sentences.text: The government has warned some schools start teaching GCSEs in the first year of secondary school Secondary schools will be told not to teach GCSEs early as part of a major shake-up of how children in Years 7 to 9 are taught in England.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The government plans to make Key Stage 3 a more distinct education phase, urging schools to focus less on exams and more on a "richer, more engaging" experience.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The changes come in response to two reviews that found pupils were increasingly becoming disengaged in their early teenage years, affecting attendance and achievement, the Department for Education (DfE) said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The move will mark a reversal of the approach taken by the previous Conservative government to focus the first three years of secondary school on core subjects and on doing well in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: Former Education Secretary Michael Gove prioritised English, maths and science, while raising grade boundaries, making exams harder and limiting resits.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: He also made GCSEs linear, meaning they are sat all in one go at the end of Year 11 instead of over the course of Key Stage 4.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: These reforms meant teachers started preparing pupils for exams at an earlier stage at the expense of teaching unexamined parts of their subject.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The DfE has pledged a "more engaging offer" in subjects like drama, PE, music and languages, which have seen a decline in students taking them, when it publishes its new curriculum later this year.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: It says persistent absence nearly doubles among pupils between Year 6 and Year 9.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The department pointed to a recent survey commissioned by the International Baccalaureate that found GCSE prep dominated Key Stage 3 learning in England, with 57% of teachers saying it was the leading influence on the curriculum.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: "The pressures of GCSEs and an overcrowded curriculum are resulting in too many children receiving a narrower offer during Key Stage 3 and being rushed towards exams without grasping the fundamentals or developing deeper understanding," Powell said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: "I'm putting a stop to that." A 2015 Ofsted report suggested that Key Stage 3 may be "wasted years", echoing the view at the time that pupils aged 11-14 lacked a clear motivation to work hard.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: However, the government faced criticism at the time that its reforms made each exam far more significant, meaning teachers refocused lessons only on what could come up in them.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: Reacting to the DfE's announcement on Sunday, Lib Dem education spokeswoman Munira Wilson MP said school was "more than drilling kids for exams" but cautioned against "micromanaging" teachers.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: She added that a new curriculum "alone won't get children back into the classroom", noting that "too many pupils are missing school because of anxiety and unmet mental health needs" while "schools can't offer more drama, music and languages without the teachers to teach them".
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: Action from "across society" is needed to help improve the educational outcomes of white working-class children, the co-chair of an independent inquiry looking into the issue has said.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: The inquiry's first report, published this summer , concluded that once-in-a-generation reforms were needed to fix a system "not serving the interests of white working-class children".
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: The next phase will focus on early years children and teenagers aged 14 to 19, aiming for a stronger start at primary school and improving older students' routes through education into successful careers.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell said she was "backing" the inquiry to "get to the heart of the barriers holding children back".
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: Inquiry co-chair and former education secretary Baroness Morris said the next phase of the inquiry's work will consider "what needs to be done".
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: "This isn't just the responsibility of schools but calls for action from across society," she said.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: The Independent Inquiry into White Working Class Educational Outcomes , external was commissioned by the multi-academy trust Star Academies, and is supported by the Department for Education.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: It spoke to thousands of young people and their parents, as well as hundreds of teachers.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: Education data about white working class pupils was also analysed as part of the year-long review, looking at the 1.25 million young people in England who are white British and in receipt of free school meals.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: The inquiry found a growing belief among white working-class families that the current education system does not guarantee future success.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: In the summer, the inquiry also acknowledged that the true scale of white working-class disadvantage is "likely to be substantially larger", as the education data they looked at did not include families who were on low incomes but did not receive free school meals.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: Since then, all families receiving Universal Credit have become eligible for free school meals .
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: Under the new phase of the inquiry, practical recommendations for government, schools, colleges and other organisations working with white working-class communities will be developed.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: This action will include a research programme looking at the routes taken by teenagers aged 14 to 19, investigating how schools can work with communities to provide clearer pathways into further study and successful employment.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: The new phase of the inquiry will also look at how schools can ensure the transition from primary to secondary school builds strong foundations.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: "Right now, too many white working-class children are falling behind at every stage of their education," Powell said.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: The prime minister said he was "on a mission" to reduce the number of young people not in education, employment or training - known as "Neet".
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: Currently, nearly a million young people are classed as Neet.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: Former minister Alan Milburn's interim report , external found that children who are not school-ready at aged four or five are nearly three times as likely to be Neet by ages 16 to 17.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: A final report by Milburn is expected to set out his recommendations for tackling the issue in the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: The culture secretary was interviewed by Laura Kuenssberg on Sunday Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has rejected accusations of politicising Remembrance Sunday after being criticised for linking the event to the UK rejoining the European Union's Erasmus scheme.
sentences.article_title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row

sentences.text: Her department announced on Saturday night that "as we mark Remembrance Sunday, Erasmus+ will give a new generation the chance to build connections across Europe".
sentences.article_title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row

sentences.text: That sparked a backlash from the Conservatives, who said "veterans did not fight for a student exchange scheme" and accused her of making an "EU membership pitch".
sentences.article_title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row

sentences.text: Nandy said she was "horrified" by the Tory response and insisted that the expanded EU scheme for study and work would help young Britons recognise wartime sacrifice.
sentences.article_title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row

sentences.text: The UK is rejoining the scheme in January , six years after leaving it as part of the Brexit deal.
sentences.article_title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row

sentences.text: On Saturday, the Department for Culture, Media and Sport drew comparisons between that scheme and events on Sunday to commemorate veterans who had died in conflict.
sentences.article_title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row

sentences.text: He said the bonds that veterans forged "run far deeper" than Erasmus.
sentences.article_title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row

sentences.text: "It is not a day for a Labour minister to try to make an EU membership pitch," he added.
sentences.article_title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row

sentences.text: Asked about the criticism on the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme, Nandy stood by her initial remarks.
sentences.article_title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row

sentences.text: "It was Winston Churchill after the Second World War who talked about extending the hand of friendship across Europe and making sure that we honoured the legacy of that generation," she said.
sentences.article_title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row

sentences.text: She said that after Brexit "we closed off opportunities for young people from this country to understand not just the impact that generation made here in the UK, but the way in which they went off and fought for the freedom of people across Europe".
sentences.article_title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row

sentences.text: Asked to respond to accusations she had chosen Remembrance Sunday to "promote part of the new deal the government has done with the EU", Nandy said she was "not choosing today or any day actually to promote a deal with the EU".

sentences.article_title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row

sentences.text: Youth groups will also get to do short exchanges in other countries, with a focus on areas of the country less engaged by Erasmus previously such as the north of England and Midlands, the government said.
sentences.article_title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row

sentences.article_title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row

sentences.text: Several universities in England have only been using below-average salaries in examples of student loan repayments on their websites, the BBC has found.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Treasury Committee chair Dame Meg Hillier, who led a recent inquiry into student loans, said some information about repayments was "misleading", including one instance where they were compared to the "cost of a daily coffee".
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: She also said the Department for Education (DfE) must include higher-salary examples on its own website, too.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: The DfE said it would review the information it provides, while universities said their websites referred to government information and would be reviewed where necessary.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Student loan repayments are tied to earnings, so the more you earn, the more you repay every month - and graduates generally go on to earn more than non-graduates.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Current and prospective students in England take out Plan 5 loans to pay for their tuition fees and living costs.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: They repay 9% of anything they earn over £25,000 for 40 years, or until the loan is paid off.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: The BBC looked at publicly available information on more than 110 university websites in England and found cases of inaccurate information about the salary at which they start repaying and the length of time they repay for.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: It also found that 12 universities only gave students worked examples of repayments based on earnings that are less than the UK average, which is £39,039.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Northumbria University's website said those graduates would be "repaying an amount less than the cost of a daily coffee" - a comparison that has been removed since the university was contacted by the BBC.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: The DfE website also only gives examples of monthly repayments for people earning up to £38,400 on other student loan plans, but does not include any real-world repayment examples for Plan 5 students.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Repayments are 9% of earnings over £25,000, so someone earning £30,000 will repay £37.50 per month, but someone earning £100,000 will repay £562.50 per month.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Megan Russon, 21, is a recently graduated tax accountant from Cannock with a starting salary of around £29,000, meaning she will repay about £30 a month.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: However, she expects to earn around £50,000 when she becomes chartered in three years' time, and will be repaying about £187 per month.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Megan owes about £62,000 after graduating from the University of Birmingham with a degree in accounting and finance Megan says universities gave examples of repayments based on earnings of between £25,000 and £45,000 at open days and said graduates "wouldn't even notice the repayments because they should be minimal".
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: "At the time, I wasn't sure what salary I was even going to be on when I graduated," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: The University of Exeter said Plan 5 loans were written off a decade earlier than they actually are, Royal Holloway and Edge Hill listed the wrong repayment thresholds, and Harper Adams said students from England were still on Plan 2 loans.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: All four universities have updated their websites since being contacted by the BBC.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: "I'm pretty shocked at what the BBC has uncovered here and I'm going to be raising it with the relevant MPs and urging them to write to the universities in their constituencies to make them step up and do a better job," Dame Meg said.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: She said the DfE should be "taking the lead" by reflecting repayments for higher earners, but that universities also "have a responsibility to the young people that they're taking on board for the three or four years of their degree".
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: England's controversial student loans system has left many graduates frustrated.

sentences.text: Concerns have been raised with the government about the amount of time primary school children are spending on a game designed to make learning times tables fun.

sentences.text: US Assistant Attorney General Colin M McDonald vowed to pursue all those involved In May 2024, Francis Mogambi arrived in the United States after winning the Diversity Visa lottery, a programme that gives people from around the world a chance to become permanent residents.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Just over two years later, the Kenyan national found himself at the centre of a US investigation into an alleged nationwide scheme to defraud the federal student aid system.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: On 19 October 2026, a grand jury in Nebraska indicted Mogambi on five counts of theft of government money and five counts of aggravated identity theft.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Prosecutors allege that, between November 2025 and May 2026, he worked with associates in Kenya to steal the identities of US citizens and use them to fraudulently enroll fictitious students in American colleges.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Once the fake students were enrolled, Mogambi allegedly diverted their financial aid payments to himself, keeping 30% and sending the remainder to his associates in Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The intended loss in his case was $20,000 (£15,000), according to prosecutors.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Court documents say Mogambi received $2,000 a week and attempted to recruit another person into the scheme.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He allegedly told the individual he needed a business that would allow him to cash larger cheques without paying taxes.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Mogambi was arrested shortly after the indictment was returned and is being held in custody pending trial.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He has not yet commented on the allegations against him.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: His case forms part of a wider US investigation, dubbed Operation Ghostbusters, into the alleged use of stolen identities to enrol fictitious students at colleges and claim federal financial aid that resulted in a loss of $130m in taxpayers funds.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: US authorities say the investigation has so far resulted in five indictments that involved Kenyan nationals, while a further 40 investigations remain open.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Hundreds of people have been affected after fraudsters allegedly stole their personally identifiable information (PII) and used it to access federal student aid.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The stolen personal information was sometimes sold online for between $4 and $8, with fraudsters targeting low-income Americans who had never had the opportunity to attend college.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: At a news conference on 29 October announcing the first charges in the investigation, Assistant Attorney General Colin M McDonald, who heads the Justice Department's National Fraud Enforcement Division, vowed to pursue those involved.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "If you steal taxpayers' dollars, if you exploit a programme meant to help students, we are resolved to find you and prosecute you," he said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The Justice Department says those behind the fraud use what is described as "super intelligence" to place fake students in classrooms and complete coursework, creating the impression that they are attending college and allowing financial aid payments to continue.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "The goal is to keep the ghost student in school as long as possible.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Semester after semester after semester stealing money from the taxpayers," McDonald said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: But the consequences extend beyond the financial losses suffered by the US government.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: People whose identities are stolen can find themselves facing unexpected student loan debts, even if they have never enrolled in college.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "His identity was stolen, his credit is now at risk, and his name is on the bill," McDonald said, describing the impact on one victim.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He also said that nearly a third of community college applicants in California in 2024 had been identified as fraudulent.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The scale of the suspected fraud is significant.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Investigators identified 830,840 potentially fraudulent Federal Student Aid identification numbers associated with nearly $130m in September and October 2026.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: They recommended that the Department of Education disable them.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The figure represents financial aid associated with potentially fraudulent accounts, not confirmed losses.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "In a flash, the money vanishes, often overseas in places like Kenya," McDonald said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The investigation has also exposed alleged financial links between the US and Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: In September, US officials travelled to Kenya to work with local law enforcement on extraditions, prosecutions and the recovery of money allegedly stolen from American taxpayers.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: With the help of Kenyan investigators, US authorities seized more than $750,000  from a cryptocurrency account belonging to a Kenyan national connected to the wider scheme.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The Justice Department described it as the first international seizure of its kind in Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The seizure was not connected to Mogambi's individual case.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: In a separate case in Virginia, prosecutors allege that a Kenyan national received more than 700 fraudulent student-aid refunds totalling approximately $1.44m.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: At least $1.3m was subsequently transferred through thousands of transactions to accounts in the US and Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Meanwhile, in New Jersey, three people have been charged with allegedly acting as money mules in a scheme to obtain more than $1m in federal student aid.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Prosecutors say they received the funds through US bank accounts, kept a portion for themselves and transferred the remainder to alleged co-conspirators in Kenya linked to a purported safari company.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: If convicted, Mogambi faces a mandatory prison term of at least 10 years, according to the Justice Department.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Authorities say those convicted will also face appropriate orders for forfeiture of assets and restitution to victims, in addition to any prison sentences.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Lydia Dibben wants more small farms around Wales growing produce Droughts and wildfires in the summer were a wake-up call, and winter flooding could leave Wales' food supply vulnerable, an expert has warned.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: The country currently imports the vast majority of its fruit and vegetables, with only 6% of those served in its schools grown in Wales.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: It is dependent on produce from parts of the world prone to droughts and fires, according to co-founder of an organisation aiming to address this.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: Duncan Fisher is behind Our Food Trust , external , which wants to build 100 farms, producing fruit and vegetables in Wales for local markets.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: Despite 90% of the country being used for agriculture , external , only about 0.1% is currently being used for horticulture , external .
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: Growers at Fisher's Wern Farm, near Newtown, Powys, said this must change if the country is to survive climate change, wars and other global disruptions to the supply chain.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "We are hugely dependent and these vegetables are coming from really vulnerable parts of the world like south Europe and north Africa - the areas most prone to drought, fires and overheating," said Fisher.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: Food security has become a hot topic , with Defence Secretary Wes Streeting saying in October people should have water, tinned goods, baby food, torches and mobile phone charging packs ready in case of emergency.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: Fisher referenced this appeal, adding the UK "has an incredibly centralised food system with 95% of the food we eat bought from nine supermarkets".
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: He said: "There's no storage, it's a just-in-time system so the food is stored in lorries moving across motorways.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "That is a security hazard because it's very vulnerable to cyber-attacks.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "If the system goes wrong, there's no resilience in it.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: The food just runs out straight away." Duncan Fisher said he has hope that Wales will be able to increase its fruit and veg growing Fisher and Sue Holbrook launched Our Food Trust about 10 years ago with the aim of growing more produce locally for local markets.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: They found one of the main barriers was stable housing for farmers.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: As Fisher explained: "If there's a high wind during the night, they need to get out there and protect things.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "If a sheep gets in, they have to get the sheep out before the entire thing is destroyed in an hour.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: So they have to live there." But he said planning regulations have made it really difficult to build homes on farmland.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: However, by working with Powys council and Bannau Brycheiniog National Park Authority, they have been able to build three temporary homes for farmers on 36 acres of council-owned land.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: They are currently building three more.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: Lydia Dibben, one of the growers, said even though it was a difficult year they were able to grow a lot of food One of the growers at Wern Farm is Lydia Dibben, 28, and she agreed access to land is one of the biggest barriers to new farmers.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: She said if her home was not provided she would have to get another job to be able to afford rent, and then would end up without enough time to farm.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "I'm only growing on about just over an acre this year, and we're now doing 50 veg boxes a week," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "We've been doing four farmers' markets a month up until the beginning of October.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: We're also supplying into regional and national wholesale as well.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "I don't know how many people we're feeding, but it's got to be hundreds of people on just a couple of acres." She believes there are lots of people who want to do similar work, and they should be given access to land and affordable housing to do so.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "We're going to have to really think a lot harder about how we're producing food, even in this country," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: This includes looking at which vegetables work best in hotter climates.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: Dibben described the past summer as the hardest she had experienced in five years of growing.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "The hours I was keeping were just insane," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "I was getting out to the field at 05:00, and then working until it got just too hot to be outside, which was like 11:00 some days, maybe even earlier." She said working in polytunnels was impossible by 09:00 due to the heat.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: When it became too hot to work, she had to go indoors and "just survive until it was cool enough to go back outside at probably 17:00".
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: She then worked until midnight to try and get everything watered.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: Dibben said she did not usually have to worry too much about not having enough water, but this year was completely different.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "Even the things that you felt like you were giving as much water as you could were still not growing as much as they should be," she added.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "Everything was slower and stunted.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "We've not had the water bill yet for this summer, but I dread to think.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "We've just not had the crops to make it worth it." Lydia Dibben said every day is different on the farm She does not believe it will necessarily be as bad every year, but Dibben accepts there will be more hot summers and unpredictable weather such as flooding.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: Dibben thinks there will always be a need for bigger scale farms producing wheat, barley, beef or sheep.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "But I think if there was a farm like ours every 10 miles throughout Wales, that would be a pretty great future in my eyes," she added.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: The Welsh government said "significant progress" had been made on its plans to create a national food strategy to "target a more resilient, integrated and sustainable food system".
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "There will also be a focus on how to grow more fruit and vegetables in Wales, and we have already begun mapping the current position of the sector with key stakeholders," said a spokesperson.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: The UK government's Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said: "We recognise the hurdles that our vital fruit and vegetable growers face, which is why we are slashing planning red tape and investing £200m to help farmers trial crop boosting technology.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: The National Trust hopes to create new wildlife habitats to attract wildlife including water vole and turtle doves A 370-acre (150-hectare) area of land on the edge of Cambridge has been returned to the care of the National Trust - for the first time in 60 years.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: The area - known as Northfield - runs alongside the opposite side of Quy Road towards Bottisham, seven miles (11km) from the city and close to Anglesey Abbey.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: The National Trust hopes to restore the natural site to create new wildlife habitats and improve community access to green space.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: Northfield is a rich natural site with a distinctive fen-edge landscape where low-lying fenland meets the higher chalk ridge Northfield has been acquired by the trust for the first time since the 1960s, following an agreement with the tenants.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: There is evidence of human activity on the site stretching back thousands of years including the Roman period.

sentences.text: The National Trust said it hoped that, over time, species such as harvest mice, water voles and turtle doves would benefit.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: Old landfill and industrial sites have been major sources of the chemicals in rivers like the Mersey Levels of the two most toxic "forever" chemicals in England's rivers have dropped by nearly a third over the last decade, according to new figures from the Environment Agency (EA).
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The decline in the chemicals, PFOS and PFOA, has been put down to stricter restrictions on their use in products after increasing evidence emerged of their damaging impact on human health and the environment.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: One expert studying the impact of the chemicals said it was "brilliant" to see how far the UK has come on this issue.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: Thousands of other forever chemicals, known officially as PFAS, remain in use but the regulator said its report showed the need for them all to be better monitored and regulated.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: PFAS were first developed in the 1930s in the US and became popular with companies making products like frying pans and firefighting foam because of their useful, oil-resistant, water-resistant and electrical properties.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: They are called forever chemicals because their natural resistance means they take a very long time to break down naturally.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The earliest types of these chemicals were called PFOS and PFOA.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: But two decades ago researchers started to find that they were linked to tissue damage in animals and increased rates of certain serious health conditions such as testicular cancer. , external As a result, PFOS was all but banned in the UK in 2010 and PFOA in 2020.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The latest data from the regulator, published on Thursday, shows that the concentrations in English rivers of PFOS and PFOA over the last 10 years have now fallen by 30% and 29% respectively.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: Levels in freshwater fish have fallen 49%.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: "It's brilliant to see how far we have come in the last 10 years," said Dr David Megson, reader in environmental forensics at Manchester Metropolitan University.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: There are thought to be around 15,000 other PFAS, although only around 200 are frequently used.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The EA said that despite increasing research into these compounds, "uncertainty remains regarding the toxicity of many PFAS".
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: It said its findings "reinforces the need" for regulating all PFAS rather than one by one.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The chemicals industry has long opposed such an approach, arguing that there is currently no, or limited, evidence to suggest that other PFAS are toxic and that some have vital uses such as in life-saving medical equipment.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The regulator is now regularly testing for 60 other PFAS to build a picture of contamination across the country, and earlier this month the government announced that it would begin monitoring levels in people's bodies.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The EA report acknowledged that while concentration levels had fallen, because the chemicals take so long to break down, the overall amount still in the environment is likely to have remained unchanged - they have simply been diluted and been washed into the sea.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: "There is a lot to do, and this report provides an essential foundation to support investigations to make the polluters pay for any damage they have caused," said Megson.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: One of the few ways to permanently destroy PFAS is by high-temperature incineration - there are currently just two such suitable sites in the country.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: They launched an investigation into Givan's Israel trip following a number of complaints and questions.
sentences.article_title: Education minister cleared over Israel trip

sentences.text: Those included whether Givan had taken the trip in his role as minister or as an MLA, the use of Department of Education resources and public funds, and whether the trip had breached the political impartiality of the civil service.

sentences.text: But the commissioner did not uphold the complaints and found that Givan had not breached the ministerial code by going on the trip to Israel.

sentences.article_title: Education minister cleared over Israel trip

sentences.text: Swans and ducks have enjoyed the wetland reserve at Slimbridge for 80 years Most people know rainforests are vital in the fight against climate change, but now scientists say wetlands could be even more important.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Saltmarshes, mangrove swamps and wetlands can absorb carbon "four times faster than trees", according to the charity the Wildfowl and Wetlands Trust (WWT).
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Celebrating 80 years since WWT's first wetland bird reserve was founded at Slimbridge, in Gloucestershire, the charity's leaders have called for one million hectares of wetlands to be restored across the world.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Sarah Fowler, CEO of WWT, said: "They are mood-boosting, flood-buffering, water-purifying, incredible habitats.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: But we have lost 85% of the world's wetlands." Sir Peter Scott feeds migrating swans and geese at Slimbridge in 1947, with Desmond Hawkins, BBC features producer from Bristol WWT now runs 10 wetland bird reserves across the UK.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Many people come to enjoy the swans, geese, flamingoes and migrating wildfowl, but do not realise how powerful these habitats can be in soaking up carbon and slowing down climate change.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: So how vital are wetlands for birds, and how powerful can they be in the fight against climate change?
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: This video can not be played The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change In November 1946, a naturalist called Peter Scott came to a wild marshy area on the banks of the River Severn, near Slimbridge.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: He was drawn by the thousands of migrating geese and swans that flew thousands of miles from the Russian Arctic to spend the winter here on the mudflats and marshes.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Captivated, Scott settled in a small cottage and later built a house right on a lake, with a huge window to watch the wildfowl.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: He dug lakes and connecting channels, built hides and even towers to watch the birds without disturbing them.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Over the years, the reserve grew and became home to thousands of ducks, swans , geese as well as the migrating wildfowl.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Sir Peter Scott with the first nine Nēnē geese he hand-reared at Slimbridge in 1952 "He really was a pioneer in conservation," said Chris Moore, a historian of Slimbridge and author of Peter Scott and the Birth of Modern Conservation.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: As well as creating a safe haven for endangered species, Scott was a vigorous campaigner for nature.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: He led the fight to stop commercial whaling, presented some of the BBC's first natural history programmes called live from Slimbridge, and helped set up WWF, the World Wildlife Fund.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: In 1973 Sir Peter Scott became the first person to be knighted for conservation work.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Moore explained: "Scott was talking about the impact that man was having on the natural world, long before we started talking about climate change and global warming.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "David Attenborough called him the Patron Saint of Conservation, and I think that is more than deserved," Moore added.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Electrical items caused fatal fire, inquest hears Councillor admits harassing bar owner Residents protest against plans for  greenbelt homes One of Scott's typically ambitious projects was to save the Hawaiian Goose, or Nēnē.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Unique to the Pacific islands, the Nēnē was hit hard by road building and development.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: By 1949 barely 24 birds remained.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Scott heard of its plight, and asked Hawaiian authorities to send a few geese to Slimbridge where he hand-reared them.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "Unfortunately they sent us two females," chuckled Enid Cole, a WWT volunteer at Slimbridge.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "Peter asked them for a gander - 'It would help', he said." Nine chicks were later born, and hand-raised successfully to adulthood at Slimbridge.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Dave Harvey helped to feed the Nēnē geese at Slimbridge Today there are more than 3,000 Nēnē geese, most of them living peacefully on Hawaiian golf courses.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: But a handful still live at Slimbridge, where Enid Cole and her friends hand feed them lettuce every day.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "It's a marvelous project, and typical of Sir Peter," Enid smiled.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Over the last 80 years, the teams at Slimbridge have hand-reared several other species, including the Common Crane and the world's rarest diving duck, the Madagascan Pochard.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: It was while they were working to save the Madagascan Pochard that they realised how vital the wetland habitats were.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "We realised that to save that species, we had to bring the wetland back," explained Sarah Fowler, WWT's chief executive.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: And yet, as Fowler explained, "40% of the world's species rely on wetland habitats for survival".
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: What started at Slimbridge has spread to 10 wetland reserves across the UK with the charity now working with local councils to restore wetlands, even in small city areas.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Wetlands are 'mood-boosting, flood buffering habitats' said Sarah Fowler, Chief Executive of WWT The Wetlands Charity A scheme in Bristol has seen small floating islands of wetland plants moored in the city's harbour.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Across the world, they are campaigning to restore one million hectares of lost wetland, partly to provide safe habitats for endangered species but also because wetlands help absorb carbon far quicker than even forests.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "Salt marshes bury carbon," said Fowler.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "Every time the big tides go over them, the plants that have grown up in the salt marsh get buried.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Those plants are full of carbon, so they are a massive carbon sink.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "And the brilliant thing about salt marshes is they do this four times faster than trees.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Wetlands are vital in our fight against climate change, and we must restore them." What started 80 years ago as a bird reserve on the banks of a river in Gloucestershire has grown into a global campaign to restore wetlands, which they call the "soggy secret weapon" against climate change.

sentences.article_title: Why Walliams' unprecedented legal battle to stay anonymous failed

sentences.article_title: Why Walliams' unprecedented legal battle to stay anonymous failed

sentences.text: This was, the court ultimately concluded, unheard of.
sentences.article_title: Why Walliams' unprecedented legal battle to stay anonymous failed

sentences.text: Under Article 2 of the European Convention on Human Rights, the British state has a duty to take reasonable steps to try to protect life where they can do so and, importantly, where a particular body has an actual responsibility to do so.
sentences.article_title: Why Walliams' unprecedented legal battle to stay anonymous failed

sentences.text: There's no expectation that a state agency can save all lives in all circumstances - but it must show it has done its best if it is clear it had a responsibility to act.
sentences.article_title: Why Walliams' unprecedented legal battle to stay anonymous failed

sentences.text: The most obvious example of this law in practice is that the police must try to act on credible intelligence of a threat to life, even if the intended victim is a gangster.
sentences.article_title: Why Walliams' unprecedented legal battle to stay anonymous failed

sentences.text: But that duty, and how it should be applied in the real world, is also why Walliams lost: he was expecting the wrong public body to be doing the protecting.

sentences.article_title: Why Walliams' unprecedented legal battle to stay anonymous failed

sentences.text: He had been detained for his own protection, meaning the state was already trying to meet its obligation to protect him from harm.
sentences.article_title: Why Walliams' unprecedented legal battle to stay anonymous failed

sentences.article_title: Why Walliams' unprecedented legal battle to stay anonymous failed

sentences.article_title: Why Walliams' unprecedented legal battle to stay anonymous failed

sentences.article_title: Why Walliams' unprecedented legal battle to stay anonymous failed

sentences.text: "It is slightly concerning that there is not an ability to proceed today.

sentences.text: I don't understand really.

sentences.text: All parties have been banned at the university Four Nigerian students have died after attending a party in the south-eastern town of Nsukka to celebrate the end of their final exams.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.text: The cause of death has not been confirmed but police spokesman Daniel Ndukwe said the two men and two women had reportedly fallen ill after consuming alcoholic drinks at the party.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.text: The University of Nigeria Nsukka has declared three days of mourning, during which academic and social activities will be suspended.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.text: The tragedy comes amid a wider crackdown on fake and adulterated alcoholic drinks in Nigeria, where the food and drug regulator has been raiding suspected producers of unsafe food and beverages.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.text: The university's Vice-Chancellor, Professor Simon Ortuanya, said the university had received a distress call at 22:00 on Wednesday, and sent security personnel to a house party at Praise Lodge, outside the campus in Nsukka's Hilltop area.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.text: "The preliminary investigation and interim report point to alleged alcohol abuse or drug paraphernalia and things like that.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.text: But we are not conclusive on those matters," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.text: He described the deaths as "tragic and painful".
sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.text: "As a community, we mourn, not just alone, we mourn with the families, the parents that have suffered these years to train the men and women in their studies," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.text: Ortuanya also announced a ban on signing-out celebrations, which are commonly held by final-year students to mark the completion of their studies.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.text: The celebrations often involve parties, dancing, photographs and friends signing one another's shirts.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.text: He urged students to use graduation as a time to reflect on their university experience and prepare for life beyond campus.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.text: The university said it was working with security agencies to establish what had caused the deaths.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.text: The police have also launched an investigation.

sentences.text: They said alcoholic drinks had been recovered from the scene and the bodies taken to a mortuary for autopsies.

sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.article_title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party

sentences.text: Beirne will captain Ireland for the second time on his 75th cap in Saturday's Nations Championship game against Fiji As Tadhg Beirne prepares to captain Ireland at home for the first time, it is worth recapping the impressive manner in which he has built up his CV in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Beirne leads Ireland bid to build on strong start

sentences.text: Since missing the final three games of the Six Nations Grand Slam campaign in 2023 with an ankle injury, Beirne has missed just three Ireland Tests.
sentences.article_title: Beirne leads Ireland bid to build on strong start

sentences.text: He was rested against Italy in 2024 and missed last year's summer meetings with Georgia and Portugal while on British and Irish Lions duty.
sentences.article_title: Beirne leads Ireland bid to build on strong start

sentences.text: Such big-game ubiquity is not easily found in the modern game - and Beirne has often delivered in red and green.
sentences.article_title: Beirne leads Ireland bid to build on strong start

sentences.text: He won the United Rugby Championship with Munster - his second league title after prevailing with Scarlets in 2017 - and was appointed the province's captain, replacing the legendary Peter O'Mahony.
sentences.article_title: Beirne leads Ireland bid to build on strong start

sentences.text: A five-Test Lion, his performances in the back row for Farrell's tourists last year in Australia - playing every minute across the Test series win over the Wallabies - earned him the player of the series accolade.
sentences.article_title: Beirne leads Ireland bid to build on strong start

sentences.text: A three-time member of World Rugby's men's 15s dream team of the year, Beirne was handed the Ireland captaincy for the first time in July's Nations Championship win over Japan, leading them to a 36-20 win.
sentences.article_title: Beirne leads Ireland bid to build on strong start

sentences.text: Next year, adding to his fond memories down under as a key part of Ireland's World Cup squad will top his priority list.
sentences.article_title: Beirne leads Ireland bid to build on strong start

sentences.text: "It's particularly special doing it at the Aviva, at home," said Beirne, who is deputising for the injured Caelan Doris and Dan Sheehan.

sentences.text: Now, with another week's training under the belt, Beirne says Ireland are determined to lay down another marker before next week's mouth-watering tussle with world champions South Africa.

sentences.text: "The big focus for us is to continue building on our performance, particularly from last week," he added.

sentences.text: MSF says that many frontline workers do not have the equipment they need Hundreds of millions of dollars meant to help tackle Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo are not reaching the intended recipients, a medical charity has warned.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: A report from Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) said that while the outbreak remained "out of control", front-line workers were going unpaid, lacked proper training and were struggling with shortages of essential supplies.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: It added that in some cases ambulances had run out of fuel.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: More than 5,400 people have died and 11,000 infected with Ebola in DR Congo since the outbreak was declared in May.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: This makes it the second-most deadly outbreak of the disease ever recorded.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: MSF has urged the Congolese government and UN agencies to "strengthen oversight and accountability" to ensure money already disbursed is effectively utilised.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: This means "ensuring response personnel are properly trained, paid, equipped, and supported, and directing resources towards areas where needs are greatest", it said.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: The BBC has asked the Congolese government for comment.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: MSF's warning adds to concerns raised by Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) last month, when it said that $700m (£527m) out of $962m disbursed to organisations implementing Ebola response was unaccounted for.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: At the time, Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya said it was too early to describe it as embezzlement, characterising the issue as a major transparency and financial reporting failure.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: The Congolese health minister echoed these concerns, saying that aid agencies were required to provide details of their work so the ministry could provide oversight but that only 22% had done so.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: "Our requirement is clear: transparency must be total.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: The response relies on a single plan, a single budget, and a single coordination," Health Minister Samuel-Roger Kamba said on X. , external What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: "Our teams are often left speechless by the dysfunctions they witness in many areas.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: Six months into the response, this situation is simply unacceptable," said MSF president Javid Abdelmoneim.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: One important way of stopping Ebola from spreading is contact tracing - finding all those people who had come into contact with an infected person and putting them into isolation.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: "Despite the resources officially allocated to this critical activity, surveillance remains deeply problematic," MSF said, adding that two-thirds of deaths were occurring in communities not treatment centres.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: According to British epidemiologist Neil Ferguson, more than half of the cases are going undetected, meaning the outbreak is likely to last another year, reports the Reuters news agency.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: MSF also raised concerns over "excessive concentration" of efforts in certain areas at the expense of other areas where needs were more urgent.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: It said the response was "too slow" in North Kivu province while Haut-Uélé remained "dramatically overlooked".
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: In both provinces, MSF observed that teams were "inadequately resourced to respond effectively" with health facilities lacking essential items such as water, chlorine or triage systems.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: "This has turned some facilities into new centres of transmission, rather than places of care that contribute to containing the disease," MSF said.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: The epicentre of the outbreak is in eastern DR Congo, which has been wracked by conflict for many decades, with some affected areas under rebel control.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: There are very few good roads in the area, making it very hard to travel around.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: On Thursday, the UN and government warned that the areas worst affected by Ebola were also suffering from a severe food crisis, with almost 10 million in the region in dire need.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: The latest outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo species of the virus, has spread beyond DR Congo borders, with cases reported in Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: On Wednesday, the last person infected with Ebola in Kenya was discharged, marking a major milestone in efforts to contain the disease in the East African nation .
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says

sentences.text: The Bundibugyo species is relatively rare and has no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.
sentences.article_title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says
